Given that $R$ is the type II region shown above, 
${∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}V=$
question.worked_solution:
For a type II region $R$ with projection $D$ onto the $yz$-plane, the triple integral of a continuous function $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ is given by

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A.
$$

We consider the region $R$ as a type II region enclosed between the back surface $x={u}_{1}(y,z)=1$ and the front surface $x={u}_{2}(y,z)=2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14231356/assets/e5779dc92c875bef280425ed24a17cfb53f9f2a9736292a92ccdb988044237a6.png)

So, the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,1\le x\le 2\}.
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I *plane* region in the $yz$-plane with the upper curve

$$
z=1-{y}^{2}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14231356/assets/00f2847a8e4c927a1c6631f4aef03c57b9d28f18341b268182501ada07225382.png)

Hence, $D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le z\le 1-{y}^{2}\}.$

Therefore, we write the triple integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}V & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{1}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{y}^{2}}[{\int }_{1}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{y}^{2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡z[x]_{x=1}^{x=2}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{y}^{2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$
